acceptance: Path 1, oracle review submitted on a batch PR: the oracle-review workflow run (job review-event, event pull_request_review) succeeds and its head_sha equals the PR head. The oracle-gate bridge run dispatches the gate for that PR. The dispatched oracle-gate (workflow_dispatch pr=N) run posts oracle-gate on the PR head, and that status's updated_at is later than the review's submitted_at. Run IDs are recorded.

Path 1b, same-head success to non-success: on a batch PR whose head already has oracle-gate success, a later oracle review on the same head with a non-success verdict (pending or failure) is followed by an oracle-gate failure newer than that review, with no close-and-reopen and no new ci.yml run. If no such review happens during the batch, record 'not observed' instead of claiming coverage.

Path 2, rejudge using the decision gate 3 procedure: record the oracle-verdict run's event, its workflow_run.head_sha against the PR head, and whether the bridge found the PR. Record whether oracle-gate was refreshed anyway through the review-submitted notification. State the decision for oracle-verdict-dispatch-gate-after-review-20261025: proceed if the verdict completion did not map to the PR, drop with evidence if it did, or 'undecided, not observable' with the reason.

Path 3, dismissal: record from GitHub's API behavior and docs whether the oracle's COMMENT reviews can be dismissed at all. If they cannot, record that the dismissed trigger covers only approvals and change requests, and update the design doc if it claims otherwise.
Path 4: make pr-rerun on a batch PR reruns failed CI jobs, or reports nothing to rerun. It never closes and reopens the PR.

Path 5: a PR whose head still carries old failed oracle-review check runs from before the cutover arms with make pr-arm, so non-required failures do not block it. Use a batch PR if one has such runs, or another PR with owner permission; otherwise record that none existed.
Record that pull_request_review edited was not exercised live, unless an oracle review edit happened during the batch.
Each result above is recorded in this item's context with run IDs or URLs before finish.
context:
Source: Advisor review ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/oracle-review-workflow-advisor-20261025/report.md, recommended plan step 6 and open questions 2-4.

Live results (2026-10-25):
- Path 1, passed, on batch PR #3430 after its rebase onto develop (head 79847678d). The oracle review was submitted at 05:01:27Z. oracle-review run 40164013965 (event pull_request_review, head_sha 79847678d equal to the PR head) succeeded with its single job review-event; the head has 0 check runs named oracle-review. Bridge run 40164166225 succeeded and dispatched the gate for #3430. Dispatched run 40164248682 succeeded, and oracle-gate posted success at 05:08:06Z, after the review. Earlier bridge runs for the same head (40164016223, 40162503530, 40162579971) were cancelled by newer ones in the bridge-<sha> group as designed.
- Path 1b, not observed: no batch PR head with oracle-gate success later received a non-success oracle review during the batch.
- Path 2, not observed on a batch PR: no /oracle-review or Dispute rejudge was needed on a batch PR. Passive, read-only supporting evidence from public run metadata, with no action taken on those PRs: issue_comment-triggered oracle-verdict runs 40162405168, 40162825446, 40162844011 and 40163535345 (PRs #3412, #3433, #3434, #3435, 04:34-04:53Z) all carry head_sha 09365c09c, develop's tip at 04:32Z, not the PR head. The bridge therefore cannot map comment-triggered verdict completions to their PR, which confirms Advisor finding F3. For pull requests whose branch predates the cutover, the gate is still refreshed through the PR's own oracle-review workflow completion.
- Decision for oracle-verdict-dispatch-gate-after-review-20261025: proceed. Its gate 1 allows 'not observable', and the notification is controlled by the pull request, which is an independent reason. The passive evidence points the same way.
- Path 3: GitHub's docs say dismissing a review changes it to a review comment, so only approvals and change requests can be dismissed (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/review-pull-requests/dismissing-a-pull-request-review). The oracle posts COMMENT reviews, so the dismissed trigger never fires for an oracle review; it covers only human approvals and change requests, which are not oracle-gate inputs. The design doc does not claim otherwise. A clarifying sentence lands with the verdict-dispatch item's PR, which edits the same doc.
- Path 4, passed: make pr-rerun PR=3429, using the reworked script, refused while CI was running. It then reran the failed jobs of run 40159508665 and all jobs of run 40159508681 (stale tooling and hold suites), without closing and reopening the PR. The same happened for #3430's stale results-data and hold suites.
- Path 5, none existed at arm time: no batch PR head carried pre-cutover failed oracle-review check runs when it was armed. #3430's old head 2fbd958f1 had them but was rebased before arming. pr-arm's refusals on #3429 and #3430 named only required suites (tooling, hold, results-data), never oracle-review.
- pull_request_review edited: not exercised live; no oracle review edit happened during the batch.

Recorded out of scope for this batch, with reasons:
- Oracle thread resolve or reopen events: GitHub has no Actions trigger for them, and the ruleset's native thread-resolution requirement blocks merging with unresolved threads.
- Runner cost of human review events: an accepted cost of keeping 'submitted'.
- Unverified external consumers of the oracle-review check name: they must read the live required checks.
- Review run subtype counts: moot, because 'submitted' is kept.
- Measured congestion: not attributable from the captured data.
- Remaining sweep-only freshness gaps, mainly schedule delay: reported to the owner as residual risk; not accepted on the owner's behalf.
description:
Problem: the cutover changes which events refresh the required oracle-gate. Unit tests cannot prove GitHub's event payloads behave as the design assumes: the head_sha of review-event runs, the bridge's develop pull request lookup, and the dispatched gate run. Advisor finding F3 is unverified: oracle-verdict runs started by an /oracle-review comment, a dispatch or the schedule may complete against develop's head SHA, so the bridge cannot map them to the pull request.

Outcome: recorded live evidence for each event path, and a recorded proceed-or-drop decision for oracle-verdict-dispatch-gate-after-review-20261025.

Decision gates:
1. Observe only pull requests opened by this batch. Use another pull request only with the owner's permission, recorded here. Never post stand-ins, close and reopen, or dismiss another session's reviews. Do not fabricate oracle verdicts.
2. If a path fails: record the evidence in context, create a follow-up item for the fix with no needs on this item, then set this item's needs to that follow-up so it finishes after the fix. Item 8 stays blocked through its need on this item. A path that cannot be observed during the batch is recorded as 'not observed' with the reason, not as passed or failed.
3. Getting a new oracle review on the same head: a plain /oracle-review comment with no 'Dispute:' reply can leave the head's decision in place (oracle-review-v2.md:508-525), and same-head reruns are limited by the daily budget and backoff. Trigger rejudges only on a head whose last result is pending, or after a 'Dispute:' reply on a thread of this batch's own PR. Confirm that the verdict run's post job posted a review, with the guard not skipped (oracle-verdict.yml:983-987). Otherwise record the path as not observable, and do not decide item 8 from it.

Item guardrails: observation only, apart from at most one docs correction PR when observed behavior contradicts docs/internal/oracle-review-v2.md. Allowed triggers are the existing ones: /oracle-review or 'Dispute:' replies on this batch's own pull requests, and gh workflow run oracle-gate.yml --ref develop -f pr=<n>.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests.
